name: bike-parking-redraft
goalText: Require bike parking at new apartment buildings

clarifyAnswers.answer: 20+ units — applies only to larger developments, easing burden on small builders
clarifyAnswers.question: What is the minimum building size that should trigger the bike parking requirement?

clarifyAnswers.answer: 1 space per 2 units (0.5:1 ratio) — moderate standard, less burden on developers
clarifyAnswers.question: How many bike parking spaces should the ordinance require per dwelling unit?

clarifyAnswers.answer: Covered and secured (e.g., locked room or cage inside the building or parking structure)
clarifyAnswers.question: What location and security standard should the ordinance require for the bike parking spaces?

clarifyAnswers.answer: New construction plus substantial renovations (e.g., permit valuations exceeding 50% of building value)
clarifyAnswers.question: Should the bike parking requirement apply to existing buildings that are substantially renovated or expanded, or only to new construction?

clarifyAnswers.answer: Allow administrative variance for documented hardship (e.g., site constraints, historic buildings)
clarifyAnswers.question: Should the ordinance allow any flexibility for developers who cannot meet the standard requirements, or should it be strictly mandatory with no exceptions?

source.title: NCGS §160D-702 — Grant of Power (Zoning Regulations)
source.excerpt: a zoning regulation may regulate and restrict the height, number of stories, and size of buildings and other structures... the location and use of buildings, structures, and land.

authority.explanation: North Carolina is a Dillon's Rule state, meaning municipalities may only act where the General Assembly has expressly granted authority. That authority is present here. NCGS §160D-702 — the core "grant of power" for municipal zoning — authorizes a local government to "regulate and restrict the height, number of stories, and size of buildings and other structures; the percentage of lots that may be occupied; the size of yards, courts, and other open spaces; the density of population; the location and use of buildings, structures, and land." A bike parking requirement is a development standard governing the location and use of structures, which falls squarely within that grant. Additionally, NCGS §160D-703(a) authorizes jurisdiction-wide development standards that apply uniformly rather than only within particular zoning districts — meaning Henderson can enact this as a citywide standard rather than a district-by-district rule. Two statutory limits deserve attention but do not block this ordinance: (1) NCGS §160D-702(b) restricts "building design elements," but that term is defined narrowly (exterior color, cladding, roof style, window placement, etc.) and does not include functional infrastructure like bike storage. A covered, secured bike room is a use-and-structure standard, not a design element. (2) SB 382 (Session Law 2024-57) restricts downzoning of existing property without owner consent, but this ordinance imposes a prospective development standard on new construction and substantial renovations — it does not rezone any existing property, so SB 382 is not implicated. No state preemption on bicycle parking has been identified. The ordinance should be enacted as an amendment to Henderson's zoning ordinance or unified development ordinance, following the legislative hearing process required by NCGS §160D-601.

comparables.quote: Uses within the SRP-C District (County Only), Downtown and Compact Neighborhood Tiers shall provide bicycle parking based on the category and square footage of each use.

source.title: Durham Unified Development Ordinance, Sec. 10.3 Required Parking

comparables.outcome: Bicycle parking is an established development standard in Durham's UDO, but it applies only within designated high-density tiers — not as a citywide standard for all residential buildings. Smaller NC cities have not followed suit with a jurisdiction-wide residential mandate, leaving Henderson as a potential first mover at its size.
comparables.headline: Bicycle parking required for residential and commercial uses within Downtown and Compact Neighborhood Tiers of the Unified Development Ordinance

comparables.quote: For an apartment building, the requirement is 1 enclosed bicycle parking space per two dwelling units.

source.title: NYC Bicycle Parking Code — Zoning Resolution §25-811
source.publisher: Ground Control Systems (reviewed against NYC Zoning Resolution, June 2026)

comparables.outcome: The 0.5:1 enclosed-space ratio mirrors the ratio Henderson has selected. NYC allows up to half of required spaces to be unenclosed, but the floor is a secure, weather-protected room or enclosure — matching Henderson's covered-and-secured standard. The 10-unit threshold is lower than Henderson's proposed 20-unit floor.
comparables.headline: Zoning Resolution requires 1 enclosed bike space per 2 dwelling units for apartment buildings above 10 units

comparables.quote: Apartment Building: 1 per 50 dwelling units [short-term]; 1 per 3 dwelling units [long-term].

source.title: City of Rockville Bicycle Parking Guide (Zoning Ordinance Art. 16)

comparables.outcome: Rockville sets a long-term (secured) ratio of 1 per 3 units — more demanding than Henderson's proposed 1 per 2 — plus a lighter short-term rack requirement. The two-tier structure (long-term for residents, short-term for visitors) is a design approach Henderson could adopt in a future amendment if the initial standard proves popular.
comparables.headline: Zoning Ordinance Article 16 requires long-term and short-term bicycle parking for apartment buildings

comparables.quote: Secure and covered long-term bicycle parking is designed for residents and employees.

source.title: City of Portland — Bicycle Parking Zoning Code Overview

comparables.outcome: Portland's code requires both short-term and long-term spaces scaled by use category. Notably, it created a phased implementation: residential developments triggered by substantial renovations are exempt until January 1, 2029 — a structural compromise that mirrors the administrative flexibility Henderson is already building in through its variance provision. The e-bike electrical outlet requirement (5% of spaces) is a forward-looking detail Henderson could note for a future revision.
comparables.headline: Zoning code mandates covered, secured long-term bicycle parking for most uses; residential renovation trigger temporarily delayed to 2029

comparables.quote: Prohibits obtaining a variance for quantity of bicycle parking.

source.title: San Francisco Planning — Bicycle Parking Requirements

comparables.outcome: San Francisco's standard is among the strictest in the country, benchmarked against Vancouver, Portland, New York, and national standards. Unlike Henderson's proposed ordinance, SF allows no administrative variance on the number of spaces — a deliberate policy choice made after finding that variance requests were being used to eliminate bike parking wholesale. Henderson's choice to allow hardship variances is common among smaller cities but worth monitoring: if variance grants become routine, the waiver process can hollow out the requirement.
comparables.headline: Planning Code §155.2 requires citywide bicycle parking for all new construction and certain renovations; variance on quantity expressly prohibited

existingLaw.text:
Henderson maintains two parallel land development documents: (1) the Henderson Zoning Ordinance (last revised Aug. 5, 2025), which governs most of the city and ETJ, and (2) the Unified Development Ordinance (UDO, adopted Dec. 9, 2024, last revised July 14, 2025), which applies to certain newer/mixed-use development patterns.

ZONING ORDINANCE — PARKING (Article 500):
- Section 501 requires off-street parking spaces for all uses; Section 510 (Table of Parking Standards) sets minimum auto parking ratios by use type. No bicycle parking is mentioned anywhere in the TOC or amendment list.
- Article 500 covers parking space dimensions (§541), surfacing (§542), satellite parking (§520), shared parking (§530), and general design (§540). None of these address bicycle parking.
- The amendment list for Article 500 reflects expansions of the Parking Overlay District but no bicycle parking additions.

UDO — PARKING AND DRIVEWAY REQUIREMENTS:
- The UDO states: "There are no minimum parking requirements. Bicycle parking shall be provided as follows." followed by Table 2-4 (Bicycle Parking Requirements).
- Table 2-4 establishes bicycle parking ratios by use type, but the specific ratios for multifamily/residential uses were not retrievable from available sources. The table is referenced alongside language that "where two standards are listed, the greater" applies.
- The UDO's bicycle parking requirement applies where the UDO governs but does not appear to govern all new apartment construction citywide, particularly projects governed under the older Zoning Ordinance rather than the UDO.

GAPS RELEVANT TO THE PROPOSED ORDINANCE:
1. The Zoning Ordinance — which covers most of the city — contains NO bicycle parking requirement of any kind for apartment buildings or any residential use.
2. Neither document specifies a coverage or security standard (covered, locked room/cage) for bicycle parking at apartment buildings.
3. Neither document sets a minimum building size threshold (e.g., 20+ units) as a trigger for bicycle parking.
4. Neither document addresses bicycle parking in the context of substantial renovations (permit valuation exceeding 50% of building value).
5. Neither document provides a variance/hardship process specific to bicycle parking.
6. The UDO bicycle parking provision (Table 2-4), even where it applies, does not specify security or coverage standards for residential bicycle parking.

draftTitle: AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE HENDERSON ZONING ORDINANCE TO ADD ARTICLE 5XX — BICYCLE PARKING REQUIREMENTS FOR MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENTS
draftBody:
AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE HENDERSON ZONING ORDINANCE TO ADD ARTICLE 5XX — BICYCLE PARKING REQUIREMENTS FOR MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENTS

The City Council of the City of Henderson, North Carolina, ordains:

─────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 1. FINDINGS AND PURPOSE
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.1. Findings and Purpose.

(a) Findings. The City Council finds that:

    (1) Providing safe, covered, and secured bicycle parking at residential developments reduces automobile dependence, supports sustainable transportation, and promotes the health and welfare of Henderson residents.

    (2) The Henderson Zoning Ordinance currently contains no bicycle parking requirement for multifamily residential uses. This ordinance addresses that gap for larger developments.

    (3) Adoption of this Article constitutes a development standard enacted pursuant to N.C. Gen. Stat. §§ 160D-702 and 160D-703(a), which authorize the City to regulate the size, location, and use of structures as a jurisdiction-wide standard.

(b) Purpose. The purpose of this Article is to require that new multifamily residential buildings of twenty (20) or more dwelling units, and qualifying substantial renovations of such buildings, provide a minimum number of covered and secured bicycle parking spaces as a condition of development approval.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 2. NEW ARTICLE 5XX — BICYCLE PARKING FOR MULTIFAMILY RESIDENTIAL DEVELOPMENTS
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.2. Applicability.

(a) New Construction. This Article applies to any new multifamily residential building containing twenty (20) or more dwelling units for which a building permit application is submitted on or after the effective date of this Ordinance.

(b) Substantial Renovations and Additions. This Article applies to any renovation, rehabilitation, or addition to an existing multifamily residential building of twenty (20) or more dwelling units when the valuation of the permitted work, as determined by the Building Official using standard cost-valuation methods, equals or exceeds fifty percent (50%) of the then-current assessed value of the existing structure as shown on the Vance County tax records. Where this threshold is met, the owner shall bring the entire building's bicycle parking into compliance with this Article.

(c) Existing Buildings Not Triggered. This Article does not require retrofit of bicycle parking in an existing multifamily building unless a substantial renovation or addition meeting the threshold in subsection (b) is undertaken.

(d) Mixed-Use Buildings. Where a building contains both multifamily residential units and nonresidential uses, this Article applies to the residential component. Bicycle parking required for the residential component shall be calculated separately from any nonresidential bicycle parking requirement that may be imposed under other provisions of this Ordinance or the Henderson Unified Development Ordinance.

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.3. Minimum Bicycle Parking Requirements.

(a) Required Spaces. Every multifamily residential building subject to this Article shall provide bicycle parking spaces at a ratio of not less than one (1) bicycle parking space for every two (2) dwelling units (0.5 spaces per unit), rounded up to the nearest whole number.

    Example: A 45-unit building requires ⌈45 × 0.5⌉ = 23 spaces.

(b) Fractional Spaces. Where calculation of the required number of spaces results in a fraction, the number shall be rounded up to the next whole number.

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.4. Location and Security Standards.

(a) General. All bicycle parking spaces required by this Article shall be:

    (1) Covered — protected from precipitation by a permanent roof or overhead structure that is part of the building or an attached structure; and

    (2) Secured — located within an enclosed space accessible only to building residents and their authorized guests, such as a locked room, locked cage, or locked enclosure inside the building's footprint or within an attached parking structure.

(b) Resident Access. The secured enclosure shall be accessible to all residents of the building. A key, key fob, access code, or equivalent credential shall be provided to each resident at no charge beyond normal lease or purchase terms.

(c) Bicycle Stalls. Each stall within the required enclosure shall be designed to accommodate a standard adult bicycle and shall include a fixed rack, hook, or stand that supports the bicycle frame and allows it to be locked by a personal U-lock or cable lock. Stalls shall not require residents to lift bicycles higher than four feet (4') above finished floor unless a mechanical assist is provided.

(d) Location Within the Site. Required bicycle parking shall be located:

    (1) On the same lot as the principal residential building it serves; and

    (2) With access that does not require a bicycle to be carried up or down more than one (1) story of stairs, unless a ramp, elevator, or equivalent accessibility feature is provided.

(e) Exterior Signage. The entrance to the secured bicycle enclosure shall be identified by a sign or marking clearly visible from the building's main common corridor or lobby.

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.5. Design and Construction Standards.

(a) Compliance with Code. All structures used to satisfy this Article, including rooms, cages, and enclosures, shall comply with the North Carolina State Building Code and all applicable fire, life-safety, and accessibility requirements.

(b) Dimensions. Each required bicycle parking space shall have minimum clear dimensions of two feet (2') in width and six feet (6') in length, with a minimum overhead clearance of seven feet (7') or sufficient clearance to accommodate the stall type used.

(c) Lighting. The interior of any required enclosure shall be continuously or motion-activated lit to a minimum of one (1) foot-candle at floor level.

(d) Drainage. The floor of any required enclosure shall be designed to prevent standing water.

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.6. Plan Submittal Requirements.

(a) Required Submittals. An applicant for a building permit subject to this Article shall submit, as part of the permit application, plans showing:

    (1) The location, dimensions, and design of the required bicycle enclosure;

    (2) The number of bicycle stalls provided;

    (3) The type of rack, hook, or stand in each stall; and

    (4) The access control method (key, fob, code, or equivalent).

(b) Zoning Compliance Permit. The Zoning Administrator shall review compliance with this Article as part of the standard zoning compliance permit review and shall not issue a certificate of zoning compliance for any building subject to this Article unless the bicycle parking shown on the approved plans meets the requirements of this Article.

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.7. Administrative Variance for Documented Hardship.

(a) Availability. An owner or developer may apply to the Zoning Administrator for an administrative variance from the requirements of this Article upon a showing of documented hardship.

(b) Grounds. Documented hardship shall be limited to the following categories:

    (1) Site constraints — physical characteristics of the lot (unusual shape, topography, soil conditions, flood zone limitations, or easements) that make it physically impracticable to provide the required spaces in compliance with Sec. 5XX.4;

    (2) Historic structures — the building is a designated local landmark or is listed on, or eligible for listing on, the National Register of Historic Places, and compliance would require alteration of a character-defining feature in a manner that the State Historic Preservation Office or the local Historic Preservation Commission determines is incompatible with the Secretary of the Interior's Standards; or

    (3) Other extraordinary circumstances — the applicant demonstrates that strict application of this Article would impose a substantial and unique practical difficulty not shared generally by other developments subject to this Article, and that the difficulty is not self-created.

(c) Application. An application for an administrative variance shall be submitted to the Zoning Administrator on a form prescribed by the Department of Development Services and shall include:

    (1) A written explanation of the claimed hardship with supporting documentation (surveys, photographs, engineering reports, SHPO correspondence, or equivalent);

    (2) A proposed alternative means of compliance, if any, that the applicant believes partially satisfies the purposes of this Article; and

    (3) The application fee established in the City's Fee Schedule.

(d) Standards for Approval. The Zoning Administrator may grant an administrative variance only upon finding that:

    (1) The hardship is documented and falls within one of the categories in subsection (b);

    (2) The hardship is not the result of the applicant's own actions or choices made after the effective date of this Ordinance;

    (3) Granting the variance is the minimum relief necessary to alleviate the hardship; and

    (4) The variance will not be contrary to the public interest or the purposes of this Article.

(e) Conditions. The Zoning Administrator may impose conditions on a granted variance, including requiring the applicant to provide a reduced number of spaces, an alternative location, or an alternative security arrangement that furthers the purposes of this Article to the greatest extent practicable.

(f) Partial Variances. A variance shall not reduce the required number of bicycle parking spaces by more than fifty percent (50%) unless the Zoning Administrator finds that full elimination of the requirement is the minimum relief necessary under the specific circumstances. Total elimination of required bicycle parking spaces shall not be granted by administrative variance; elimination requires action by the Board of Adjustment under the general variance procedures of [cite existing UDO/Zoning Ordinance variance section].

(g) Appeal. A decision of the Zoning Administrator on an administrative variance application under this Article may be appealed to the Board of Adjustment pursuant to N.C. Gen. Stat. § 160D-705 and the applicable procedures of this Ordinance.

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.8. Maintenance.

The owner of a multifamily residential building subject to this Article shall maintain required bicycle parking spaces, enclosures, lighting, and access control in good working order throughout the life of the building. Failure to maintain required bicycle parking constitutes a violation of this Article subject to enforcement under [cite existing enforcement/penalties section].

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.9. Relationship to the Henderson Unified Development Ordinance.

Where a multifamily residential development is subject to the Henderson Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) and the UDO contains a bicycle parking requirement applicable to that development, the more protective standard — the one that results in more bicycle parking spaces, more stringent security, or greater coverage — shall govern. The requirements of this Article and the UDO are not mutually exclusive; this Article shall not be read to reduce any requirement imposed by the UDO.

─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 5XX.10. Definitions.

As used in this Article:

"Bicycle parking space" means a space designed to accommodate one standard adult bicycle in a secure, covered enclosure as described in Sec. 5XX.4.

"Covered" means protected from precipitation by a permanent roof or overhead structure that is architecturally integrated with or structurally attached to the principal building or parking structure on the same lot.

"Dwelling unit" means a room or suite of rooms used or intended to be used as a single housekeeping unit, as defined in [cite existing definitions section of the Zoning Ordinance].

"Multifamily residential building" means a building containing three (3) or more dwelling units, including apartment buildings, condominiums, and mixed-use buildings with residential units, as may be more specifically defined in [cite existing use classification section].

"Secured" means accessible only by residents and their authorized guests through a physical or electronic access-control device (lock, key fob, access code, or equivalent) and enclosed on all sides by walls, fencing, or mesh of sufficient strength to deter unauthorized entry.

"Substantial renovation" has the meaning given in Sec. 5XX.2(b).

─────────────────────────────────────────────

SECTION 3. AMENDMENT TO ARTICLE 500 TABLE OF CONTENTS
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Article 500 of the Henderson Zoning Ordinance (Parking) is hereby amended to add the following entry to its table of contents:

{+Article 5XX. Bicycle Parking Requirements for Multifamily Residential Developments+}
{+Sec. 5XX.1. Findings and Purpose+}
{+Sec. 5XX.2. Applicability+}
{+Sec. 5XX.3. Minimum Bicycle Parking Requirements+}
{+Sec. 5XX.4. Location and Security Standards+}
{+Sec. 5XX.5. Design and Construction Standards+}
{+Sec. 5XX.6. Plan Submittal Requirements+}
{+Sec. 5XX.7. Administrative Variance for Documented Hardship+}
{+Sec. 5XX.8. Maintenance+}
{+Sec. 5XX.9. Relationship to the Henderson Unified Development Ordinance+}
{+Sec. 5XX.10. Definitions+}

─────────────────────────────────────────────

SECTION 4. EFFECTIVE DATE AND PROCESS
─────────────────────────────────────────────

Sec. 4.1. Legislative Hearing. Before final adoption, this Ordinance shall be referred to the Henderson Planning Board for a recommendation and shall be the subject of a duly noticed public hearing before the City Council, as required by N.C. Gen. Stat. § 160D-601.

Sec. 4.2. Effective Date. This Ordinance shall take effect upon adoption by the City Council and publication as required by N.C. Gen. Stat. § 160A-75, or on [EFFECTIVE DATE TO BE SET BY COUNCIL], whichever is later.

Sec. 4.3. Severability. If any provision of this Ordinance or its application to any person or circumstance is held invalid by a court of competent jurisdiction, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.

─────────────────────────────────────────────
BRACKETED PLACEHOLDERS FOR ATTORNEY REVIEW
─────────────────────────────────────────────

The following items require confirmation against the current codified text before final adoption:

[1] Article number "5XX" — assign the next available article number in Article 500.
[2] Sec. 5XX.7(f) — cite the correct section number for Board of Adjustment general variance procedures.
[3] Sec. 5XX.8 — cite the correct enforcement/penalties section of the Zoning Ordinance.
[4] Sec. 5XX.10, "Dwelling unit" definition — cite the correct existing definitions section.
[5] Sec. 5XX.10, "Multifamily residential building" definition — confirm against existing use classifications; adjust to avoid conflict with the UDO's residential use table.
[6] Sec. 4.2 — set the specific effective date, or confirm reliance on the statutory publication-and-adoption rule.

checks.note: The draft handles the dual-document problem (Zoning Ordinance vs. UDO) in Sec. 5XX.9 with a 'more protective standard governs' rule, which is a reasonable approach. However, the UDO's Table 2-4 ratios for multifamily were not retrievable — before adoption, confirm that the 0.5:1 ratio in this ordinance is not lower than whatever Table 2-4 already requires for UDO-governed projects, which could create an unintended floor reduction for those projects. checks.note: The core policy choices are well-grounded in comparables. The 0.5:1 enclosed-space ratio matches NYC's Zoning Resolution §25-811 exactly. The covered-and-secured standard mirrors Portland and NYC. The substantial-renovation trigger parallels Portland's approach. The administrative variance mechanism is consistent with smaller-city practice. One forward-looking note: San Francisco's experience shows that a variance process can hollow out the requirement over time — consider adding an annual reporting requirement (e.g., number of variances granted) so the Council can monitor whether the hardship process is being used as intended.

checks.note: The draft covers definitions, enforcement hook, effective date, scope, plan submittal, and variance — strong overall structure. Three gaps to address: (1) There is no visitor or short-term bicycle parking requirement; Rockville and Portland use a two-tier model (long-term secured for residents, short-term racks for guests) — consider whether Henderson wants to add even a minimal guest-rack requirement now or explicitly defer it. (2) The 'Dwelling unit' and 'Multifamily residential building' definitions contain unresolved cross-reference placeholders ([4] and [5]) — if the existing Zoning Ordinance definition of 'multifamily' starts at 3 units but this Article's threshold is 20 units, the mismatch could cause interpretive confusion; clarify in the definition or in Sec. 5XX.2. (3) Sec. 5XX.8 maintenance obligation has no inspection trigger or frequency — consider adding a periodic inspection right for the Zoning Administrator or tying enforcement to complaint-based inspection to give the maintenance duty teeth.
checks.label: Completeness

source.title: City of Rockville Bicycle Parking Guide (Zoning Ordinance Art. 16)
source.excerpt: Apartment Building: 1 per 50 dwelling units [short-term]; 1 per 3 dwelling units [long-term].

checks.note: The draft is well-organized and the section hierarchy is logical. Two clarity issues to fix: (1) The inline example in Sec. 5XX.3(a) (the ceiling-function notation '⌈45 × 0.5⌉ = 23') is mathematically correct but the special character may not render in all codification systems — replace with plain prose: 'Example: A 45-unit building requires 23 spaces (45 × 0.5 = 22.5, rounded up).' (2) Sec. 5XX.7(f) creates a two-step rule — administrative variance cannot eliminate spaces, full elimination requires Board of Adjustment action — but the cross-reference is a placeholder. Until that cite is filled in, a reader cannot follow the appeal path. Prioritize resolving bracket [2] before the public hearing so the variance section is self-contained and enforceable as written.
checks.label: Clarity

checks.note: The ordinance is written in standard municipal-code style throughout: declarative present tense, defined terms used consistently, no campaign language or first-person advocacy framing. The Findings in Sec. 5XX.1(a) are factual and policy-neutral. The only minor stylistic note: the phrase 'at no charge beyond normal lease or purchase terms' in Sec. 5XX.4(b) is slightly informal — consider 'without additional charge beyond the resident's standard lease or purchase agreement' for consistency with code register.
checks.label: Voice
